text.title: AI Feature Brief Extension Pack Core Rules
text.summary: Four testable rules every AI extension pack enforces.

rule.statement: Model section pins name + version + provider + deprecation_window AND fallback_chain. "Latest claude" is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Floating model names = silent regression on provider updates.

rule.statement: Eval section pins golden_set_version + pass-rate threshold + ci_width + eval_method_ref. No "we'll test it manually".
rule.rationale: Without versioned eval, promotion decisions are guesswork.

rule.statement: Hallucination policy section enumerates risk classes (factual-with-source, numerical-summary, legal-implication, …) and picks one of {refuse, caveat, fall-through-to-human} per class. No "model decides".

rationale.source: EU AI Act Article 13; product safety practice

rule.rationale: Implicit policy means undefined behaviour at the worst moment.

rule.statement: Cost section names per-request soft cap, per-day hard cap, outlier-alert threshold, billing_owner. Unspecified caps = unbounded spend.

rationale.source: FinOps for ML; provider billing surprises 2026

rule.rationale: Without caps a runaway loop costs five-figure invoice in hours.

rule.statement: The four sections are appended to a verified base PRD (problem, user, scope, success criteria present) in the same versioned store — never drafted as a standalone document. With no base PRD the pack MUST NOT be started: escalate to the PRD author. When the base PRD exists and all four sections hold concrete values, the extended brief is published only after product, engineering and finance each sign the review-log entry; one missing signature blocks publication.

rationale.source: Cagan, Inspired (2nd ed.); 04-procedure step 1 and step 5 of this methodology

rule.rationale: The pack answers "how does this AI feature fail and what does it cost" for a feature the base PRD already defines; without the base, the model, eval and cost sections have no scope to bind to and get rewritten once the PRD lands. Cagan's Inspired makes the same point for any spec: the problem and success criteria come first, the implementation constraints attach to them.

rule.statement: When any of the four sections is unanswerable with a concrete value, the brief MUST NOT be routed to review. The author logs which section blocks, the owner who supplies the input, and the missing prerequisite artefact (model catalogue, eval set with golden answers, hallucination policy template, or cost dashboard). "TBD", "latest", "we'll test manually" and "model decides" count as unfilled, not as answers.

rationale.source: Pineau et al. 2020, ML reproducibility checklist; 04-procedure step 5 decision gate

rule.rationale: A review of a half-filled brief produces sign-off on the filled sections and silence on the rest, and the silent section is the one engineering discovers in production. Naming the blocking input and its owner turns a vague "not ready" into a work item; Pineau et al. (2020) show the same pattern for eval reproducibility — an unstated eval set is an eval that cannot be re-run.

example.code: chosen_model: claude-sonnet-4 provider: anthropic fallback_chain: [claude-sonnet-3.7, gpt-4o] deprecation_window_months: 12
